paper_metadata.title: Novel Cell-AGC Technique for Burst-Mode CMOS Preamplifier With Wide Dynamic Range and High Sensitivity for ATM-PON System
paper_metadata.abstract: We propose a novel cell-AGC technique for an ATM-cell-based burst optical receiver on a 156-Mb/s subscriber system. The cell-AGC controls transimpedance gain according to the burst-cell power and enables reception of burst signals with low extinction ratio. In addition, to realize high sensitivity, we developed an amplifier that is stable under changes in ambient conditions and deviations of transistor characteristics on IC. By adopting these techniques in a CMOS preamplifier IC, the detectable power difference between burst cells was enlarged to more than 30 dB, and the minimum sensitivity was improved to less than 39.3 dBm. These performances show that our new IC fully satisfies the high-sensitivity specification of an ATM-PON system, and incorporating this IC in the system makes it more Fig. 1. Configuration of ATM-PON system. flexible and economical.

sections.title: SUMMARY
sections.text_preview: We have proposed a novel cell-AGC technique for a burst optical preamplifier in a 156-Mb/s ATM-PON system. By adopting this technique, we can realize 1) a high loud/soft ratio, 2) fast response from the first bit, 3) the ability to receive signals with an extinction ratio as low as 10 dB.
